correctness.rationale: For every existing AD(n,mu), n>=3, the point/block distance matrix decomposes on the zero-sum subspace into r-1 parallel scalar sectors, v-1 blocks of size two, and one contrast scalar. The incidence identities NN^T=nmu I+lambda J and N^TN=nmu I+mu(J-P) fix all multiplicities. The constant contrast is strictly negative up to p_par by a convex quadratic with both endpoint values explicitly negative. The two-dimensional determinant s(3^p-1)^2<=2^(3p) has exactly one sharp root. Integrality mu≡1 (mod n-1) and two quantified mean-value inequalities prove mu=1 has only the parallel endpoint, whereas mu>1 has only the transversal endpoint. This proves all p, strictness, exact nullity, squared Euclidean embedding dimensions and asymptotic. An independently enumerated 5-geometry numerical checker corroborates entire compressed spectra (up to 280 vertices), with separate shortest path BFS checks for four geometries. Remaining limitation: finite checks are auxiliary, not proof of any infinite statement.

value.rationale: This completes a natural sharp negative-type embedding invariant over the entire existing affine resolvable 2-design family with n>=3, not one selected numerical graph. The high-index case has a new transcendental threshold, a distinct incidence-coupled nullspace of dimension v-1 versus r-1 in affine planes, an exact least squared-Euclidean dimension and an analytic high-index decay law. A parameter-integrality argument prohibits equality of two competing spectral obstructions; the n>=3 dichotomy is a structural finite-geometry result. It is not a mere restatement of Ma’s ordinary-distance spectrum.
